about: The live miss: a recommendation that turns AND into OR, citing beside the rule a weaker claim ('consider dual-fuel in very cold climates') that seems to cover one branch. Advice to consider does not license choosing, so the OR recommendation still does not follow.

findings.title: Rebate guide
findings.content: Rebate guide. If your home has a heating load over 40,000 BTU/hr and is in a cold climate with a design temperature below 5°F, pair a heat pump with a gas furnace (dual-fuel) to maximize rebates and comfort.

findings.title: Installer advice
findings.content: Installers suggest that homeowners in very cold climates consider a dual-fuel system.

findings.title: What dual-fuel is
findings.content: A dual-fuel system pairs an electric heat pump with a gas furnace that takes over in extreme cold.

claims.claim: A home with a heating load over 40,000 BTU/hr in a cold climate with a design temperature below 5°F should pair a heat pump with a gas furnace (dual-fuel).
